source.title: Vitruvias Therapeutics, Inc Issues Nationwide Recall of One Lot of Thyroid Tablets, USP 30 mg Due to Potential Super Potency

sentences.sentence: Vitruvias Therapeutics announced a recall of one lot of Thyroid Tablets, USP 30 mg in the US on 21 August 2026 because testing confirmed the product could be superpotent.
Vitruvias Therapeutics announced the recall on 21 August 2026 and the US FDA posted it on 24 August 2026.
It covers one lot, number 504950, of Thyroid Tablets, USP 30 mg, because of possible superpotency.
The notice says too much thyroid hormone can cause symptoms of an overactive thyroid.
This is a US recall; UK medicines alerts come from the MHRA.

Vitruvias Therapeutics announced on 21 August 2026 a nationwide recall in the US of one lot of Thyroid Tablets, USP 30 mg, and the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) published the notice on 24 August 2026.
The recalled lot is number 504950, and the recall is to consumer level.
The reason given is that testing confirmed the product could be superpotent.
The notice says the company has received no reports of adverse events linked to the recall.
The notice says superpotent thyroid tablets can cause symptoms of an overactive thyroid, such as weight loss and changes in heart rate.
It describes older adults, pregnant women and infants as more vulnerable, especially with long-term use.
The notice says people currently using this lot should not stop without first talking to their healthcare provider, who can advise on next steps or a replacement prescription.
The FDA has said that animal-derived (desiccated) thyroid medicines are unapproved, meaning the agency has not reviewed them for safety, effectiveness or quality.
This is a US recall notice; any UK action on medicines is decided separately by the MHRA.
The US CDC's outlook dated 23 September 2026 expects the peak of combined COVID-19, flu and RSV hospital admissions to be similar to last season, with low to moderate confidence.
The CDC published its 2026-2027 Respiratory Disease Season Outlook on 23 September 2026.
It expects the combined peak hospitalisation rate for COVID-19, influenza and RSV to be within 20% of the 2025-2026 peak.
The CDC calls the outlook high-level information, not a forecast, and says it may change.
This outlook describes the US, not the UK.
The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) published a 2026-2027 Respiratory Disease Season Outlook dated 23 September 2026.
The CDC describes it as high-level information on how the season could unfold, and says it is not a forecast.
It expects the peak combined hospitalisation rate for COVID-19, influenza and RSV to be within 20% of the 2025-2026 peak, with low to moderate confidence.
For influenza, the CDC says there is no evidence that a high-severity season is more likely this year.
For RSV, it notes that the 2025-2026 peak came later than in earlier seasons and that the cause of the late peak is unclear.
The CDC lists a higher peak as a risk, driven by viruses that evade existing immunity or by lower vaccine uptake or effectiveness.
This outlook describes the US season; UK figures and vaccination advice come from UKHSA and the NHS.

source.title: FDA approves gedatolisib with fulvestrant, with or without palbociclib, for HR-positive, HER2-negative locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer

sentences.sentence: The US FDA approved gedatolisib (Revtorpyk) on 14 July 2026 with fulvestrant, with or without palbociclib, for certain HR-positive, HER2-negative breast cancers.
The US FDA approved gedatolisib (Revtorpyk, Celcuity) on 14 July 2026.
It is used with fulvestrant, with or without palbociclib, in adults with HR-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer without a detectable PIK3CA mutation.
The approval rests on the VIKTORIA-1 trial.
This is a US decision; UK availability is decided separately.
On 14 July 2026 the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved gedatolisib (Revtorpyk, Celcuity) in combination with fulvestrant, with or without palbociclib.

It is approved for adults with HR-positive, HER2-negative locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer that has no detectable PIK3CA mutation and has progressed after at least one line of endocrine therapy.

The FDA says efficacy was evaluated in VIKTORIA-1, an open-label study in which patients were randomly assigned to gedatolisib with fulvestrant and palbociclib, gedatolisib with fulvestrant, or fulvestrant alone.
The approval letter requires a further randomised trial to characterise known serious risks, including severe stomatitis and mucosal inflammation.
This is a US decision; availability in the UK is decided separately by the MHRA and NICE.
